Quick answer: The best AI automation agency for most businesses is ManasFlow for end-to-end strategy, build, and maintenance. For enterprise RPA at scale, UiPath and Automation Anywhere are the market leaders. For AI-native growth marketing, RZLT is the specialist. For Make and n8n builds, Makeitfuture and Flowmondo are the specialists, and XRAY publishes its hourly and monthly rates on its own homepage. The right choice depends on whether you need a partner (the agency handles strategy through maintenance) or a platform (you build with vendor tooling your team manages).

Disclosure: ManasFlow publishes this list, and we rank ourselves first. We show our full ranking criteria below, disclose what we could and could not verify for every agency including our own, and list honest reasons to skip us if we are not the right fit. Judge our entry by the same evidence bar we hold every other agency to.

The best AI automation agencies in 2026 are ManasFlow for full-service strategy, build, and maintenance under one roof; RZLT for AI-native growth marketing; Kanerika for data analytics paired with automation; Makeitfuture and Flowmondo for Make, n8n and Airtable builds; XRAY for teams that want published pricing before the first call; Ema AI for no-code AI employee deployment; Sana Labs for knowledge and learning agents; and UiPath or Automation Anywhere if what you actually want is an enterprise RPA platform rather than a partner.

The decision that matters most is partner vs platform. Agencies build and run your automation stack for a project fee. Platforms hand you tooling with licensing that starts around $25/month for entry tiers and climbs into custom enterprise quotes once you need real throughput, and you still need internal engineers to build with it. Picking the wrong side of that line costs months of budget and half-built integrations.

This guide compares the 12 best AI automation agencies for enterprise teams in 2026. We cover what each agency specializes in, how they price their services, and which type of organization gets the most value from each partner.

Ready to hire, or still comparing? This guide is built for research: it ranks and compares the top AI automation agencies so you can shortlist with real evidence before you talk to anyone. If you already know you want to hire an AI automation agency and you are ready to scope a project, skip ahead to our AI automation agency page for pricing structure, process, and how an engagement starts with ManasFlow.
What does an AI automation agency do?

An AI automation agency builds and runs automations that combine workflow tools such as n8n or Make with AI models, so a business process runs with less manual work. An engagement usually starts with an audit of one process, ships a first workflow, and moves to a maintenance retainer once the system runs in production. At ManasFlow the first workflow goes live one to two weeks after the audit. That is the line between an agency and an AI platform: an agency is a team that builds for you, a platform is software your team builds with.
How we ranked these agencies

We evaluated agencies on four criteria: (1) Production focus: do they build automation that survives real data, volume, and failure, or stop at the demo? (2) Stack breadth: do they cover workflow orchestration (n8n, custom code) through AI agents and RAG pipelines? (3) Pricing transparency: have they published real numbers or given honest signals? (4) Delivery languages: do they serve non-English-speaking teams? ManasFlow is listed first because it is ours and we meet all four criteria; every other agency was evaluated by the same rubric regardless of our interest.

What we checked directly: each agency's own pricing and services pages, and each agency's public review profiles. Clutch pages for ManasFlow, RZLT, Kanerika, LowCode Agency, and LeewayHertz were re-verified live on September 1, 2026. G2 pages for UiPath, Automation Anywhere, and Sana Learn blocked automated access on this pass, so those figures are carried over from our last successful pull (July 20, 2026) rather than restamped without a fresh check. What we could not verify: private client references, win rates, or delivery timelines that aren't published anywhere public. Where a rating or price wasn't publicly confirmable, we say so instead of guessing. On September 5, 2026 we re-confirmed all 9 agencies listed at the time are still live and operating (ManasFlow, RZLT, Kanerika, Ema AI, Sana Labs, UiPath, Automation Anywhere, LowCode Agency, and LeewayHertz); no pricing or review figures were re-pulled on this pass. On September 26, 2026 we added Makeitfuture, Flowmondo, and XRAY. For those three we read each agency's own website only, we did not pull review profiles, and every figure in their entries is the agency's own published claim. No hands-on testing is claimed for any entry.

1. ManasFlow, best overall AI automation agency for enterprise teams

As a workflow automation agency, ManasFlow specializes in custom workflow automation using n8n, AI agent development for autonomous business processes, and RAG pipeline architecture for connecting LLMs to private enterprise data. Their fractional CAIO (Chief AI Officer) model gives enterprises executive-level AI strategy without the full-time C-suite hire.
Not on adjectives, on checkable evidence:

Named client work with verified numbers: a legal and compliance automation build that saved a client an estimated €10,000 in fines by catching filing errors before they became penalties, a marketing operations build that automated 95% of a client's recurring campaign tasks, and a customer support automation that moved a client to 24/7 first-response coverage. These are the same case studies published on our service page, not new numbers invented for this list.

An engineer-placement model most agencies on this list do not offer: an embedded AI engineer from $60,000 a year, a 2 to 4 week placement window, and a 90-day replacement guarantee for teams that need capacity instead of a single project.
Multilingual delivery (English, French, Arabic), which matters for the non-English-speaking teams we score every agency on in our ranking criteria above.

3. Kanerika, best for data analytics paired with AI automation

Kanerika is a global consulting firm that combines AI/ML implementation with data analytics, governance, and RPA. Their strength is helping enterprises that need both data infrastructure and automation built in parallel. If your automation bottleneck is messy data rather than workflow logic, Kanerika addresses both sides.

They also offer proprietary AI products: Karl (a data insights AI agent), DokGPT (document intelligence), and FLIP (a low-code DataOps platform). This gives clients pre-built tools to complement custom consulting work.

4. Makeitfuture, best for Make and n8n automation with EU data residency

Makeitfuture is an AI automation agency that says it helps businesses "plan, build and run AI agents, workflow automations and custom integrations." It lists offices in London, Paris, and Cluj-Napoca, and builds inside Make, n8n, Zapier, Airtable, HubSpot, and boost.space rather than moving clients onto a new platform.

Its homepage reports 15,000+ AI automations, 500+ clients, and 7+ years of experience, and displays a Make Platinum partner badge and an ISO 27001 badge. Those are the agency's own figures; we did not verify them independently. It also develops custom Make and n8n apps (connectors), which matters when the tool you need has no native integration.

5. Flowmondo, best for Airtable and no-code automation in technical service firms

Flowmondo is a UK-registered automation agency that calls itself "the AI solutions partner for technical service firms." It builds software integration, process automation, AI integration, data management, document automation, and no-code apps on Airtable, Fillout, Make, n8n, Zapier, and Xano.

Its homepage describes "a dedicated team of 17 pragmatic AI and automation experts with over 2,900+ solutions delivered," 13 years trading, and more than 975 customers worldwide. Work is sold through five named methods, from InstantBuild for a fast single automation to Transform for continuous change programs. These are the agency's own figures, not independently verified.

6. XRAY, best for published hourly and monthly pricing

XRAY is a workflow design agency that says it designs "intelligent ways of working with AI and automation for purpose-led teams." It puts its rates on its homepage: XRAY Hourly at $250 per hour and XRAY Monthly at $15,000 per month.

The hourly plan is a "Done with You" model where you pair with an expert by the hour with no long-term commitment. The monthly plan is full service: XRAY owns discovery, design, execution, change management, and maintenance, with a dedicated executive strategist, workflow consultant, and project manager. It also runs workshops and ships its own products, including XR Guardian for managing no-code and low-code automations and XR Debrief for meeting summaries.

7. Ema AI, best for no-code AI employee deployment

Ema AI takes a different approach to enterprise automation: instead of building workflows, you deploy "AI employees." Their Generative Workflow Engine (GWE) powers pre-built persona templates that handle customer support, compliance analysis, HR tasks, and more. You pick a template, fine-tune it through a guided conversation, and deploy.

Founded in 2023 by former Coinbase CPO Surojit Chatterjee and backed by $61M in funding from Accel, Section 32, and KPMG, Ema targets enterprises that want to add AI capacity without writing code or managing complex integrations.

8. Sana Labs, best for knowledge management and AI learning agents

Sana Labs sits at the intersection of enterprise learning and AI automation. Their platform combines an AI-native learning management system (Sana Learn) with a no-code agent builder (Sana Agents) that connects to 100+ applications. Acquired by Workday for approximately $1.1 billion in late 2025, Sana now operates within the Workday ecosystem.
This makes Sana a strong pick for enterprises already using Workday, or those where knowledge management and employee training are core automation priorities alongside operational workflows.
